### Observed differences

- A22 was executed once in every trace in the earlier window (participation 100%); in the later window it appears in only about 53 in 100 traces, still once per trace where present. [OCC001]
- Four activities that were not observed at all in the earlier window — A27, A28, A33 and A34 — each appear in about 47 in 100 traces in the later window (94 of 200), exactly once per trace where present. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A21's outgoing transitions changed: earlier every one went to A22; in the later window about 53% still go to A22, while the remaining 47% are split across the four new activities (roughly 10–15% each). [DIR002]
- The four new activities run as a group: each pair of them co-occurs in about 47% of traces (they never co-occurred before) and appears in both orders in similar shares (about 20–27% each way), so no fixed order is observable inside the group; each of them precedes A23 in about 47% of traces. [REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030]
- A22 and the new group are mutually exclusive: A22 never co-occurs with any of the four new activities, A21 runs without A22 in about 47% of traces (previously always with it, in the order A21 then A22), and A23 now occurs without A22 in about 47% of traces (previously A22 always preceded it). [REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- The distance from A21 to A23 was always 2 event positions in the earlier window; in the later window it is 2 in about 53% of traces and 5 in about 47%, consistent with four events sitting between the two. [LAG001]
- Two smaller differences: A06's outgoing transitions shifted toward A07 (about 26% before versus 47% after, with A08 and A09 declining), and A23's mean relative position moved slightly later (about 0.53 to 0.55). [DIR001, POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, roughly every second case replaces the step A22 with a group of four new activities — A27, A28, A33 and A34 — executed between A21 and A23: A21 (present in all traces in both windows) leads into the group in about 47% of cases, the four activities each run once in no fixed order, the group precedes A23, and A22 is skipped; in the remaining cases the original A21 → A22 → A23 sequence continues unchanged. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR002, REL011, REL016, REL017, REL021, LAG001]

Supporting signs: the participation, routing, co-occurrence and distance evidence all describe the same underlying difference, each item is backed by 94–200 traces, and the 47 qualifying items far exceed the roughly 0.5 expected by chance for the 104 tested units, so sampling variation cannot account for the evidence as a whole. [OCC001, DIR002, LAG001, REL025]

Limitations and competing explanation: the internal sequence of the new group is not fixed (both orders occur for every pair), so no exact ordering constraint inside it can be stated; zero participation in the earlier window strictly means the four activities were only not observed there, so a pre-existing but unexercised branch cannot be fully ruled out; and the evidence cannot indicate why a case takes one route or the other. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030]

Other differences: A06 now routes to A07 in about 47% of its outgoing transitions versus about 26% before (A08 and A09 decline), and A23 sits slightly later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.53 to 0.55); the evidence does not tie these to the A22/new-group change, although the position shift is consistent with traces becoming longer when the group runs. [DIR001, POS001]
